title: Virtual cards in Egypt for online payments
summary: Grey, EverTry, Card-Y, Fyatu, and AstroPay: Here is how virtual cards work for online payments in Egypt and your top options.
body_markdown:
It is one thing to have the funds for online payments; it is another thing to have the means to complete the payment without getting frustrated. Managing international payments in Egypt can be quite a hassle. If you’ve tried paying for an international subscription, a work tool, online shopping, or an online course from Egypt, perhaps you can relate to the struggle. Local Egyptian bank cards are often restricted from international transactions, offer poor exchange rates, or aren’t supported by global platforms.


Virtual cards exist mostly to solve these problems, and they have become one of the most efficient options for anyone who shops online, pays for subscriptions, or needs a reliable way to spend in foreign currency without the limitations of a standard local bank card.


This article explains how virtual cards work, who they are for, and the main options available to people in Egypt right now.


## What is a virtual card, and how does it work?


A[virtual card](https://grey.co/cards) is a digital payment card that works just like a traditional debit or credit card, except it exists only electronically. Instead of receiving a plastic card, you get the card details instantly on your phone or computer, including the card number, expiration date, and CVV security code.


Because virtual cards are issued digitally, they are typically available within minutes, unlike physical cards that must be printed and delivered.


Most virtual cards operate as prepaid or debit cards, meaning you spend funds you already have. In many cases, the card is connected to a[multi-currency account](https://grey.co/) , so payments are deducted directly from your balance in currencies such as USD, GBP, or EUR. This eliminates the need to manually top up the card before each purchase.


For example,[Grey virtual cards](https://grey.co/cards) are linked directly to your foreign currency balance, allowing you to pay online or in apps without transferring funds to the card first.


In practice, using a virtual card is no different from using a physical one. You simply enter the card details at checkout when making online payments, subscriptions, or international purchases. Many virtual cards can also be added to[Apple Pay or Google Pay](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-add-your-grey-card-to-apple-pay-or-google-pay) , enabling secure[contactless payments](https://grey.co/blog/best-ways-to-make-contactless-payments-while-travelling) with your phone wherever mobile wallets are supported.

## What to look for when choosing


Not all virtual cards work the same way. The best option for you will depend on how you plan to use it, which currencies you deal with most often, and how frequently you make international payments. Before choosing a provider, it’s worth looking closely at a few key factors.


**Currency support.** Many virtual cards are designed primarily for USD payments, but international platforms often charge in other currencies such as EUR or GBP. If you regularly use services based in Europe or the UK, a card that supports multiple currencies can help you avoid additional conversion fees. Choosing a provider with a multi-currency account allows you to hold and spend different currencies more efficiently.


**Funding options.** Different platforms allow you to add funds in different ways. Some accept local bank transfers, others allow crypto deposits such as USDT, and some link directly to a multi-currency account balance, like[Grey](https://grey.co/cards) . Before signing up, check that the funding method available actually works for your situation and location.


**Platform compatibility.** Not every virtual card works equally well across all international platforms. Some services, particularly advertising platforms or large marketplaces, may reject certain cards depending on the issuing network or region. If you plan to use your card for a specific purpose, such as paying for Google Ads or cloud hosting, it’s worth confirming that the card is widely accepted on those platforms.


**Fees and exchange rates.** Virtual card costs can vary significantly between providers. Some charge a card creation fee, others add transaction fees, and most apply a small markup on currency conversions. A card that appears free at first glance may become more expensive if the exchange rate spread is high. Always look at the total cost of using the card, not just the upfront fee.


**Security and regulation.** Security should always be a priority when choosing a financial platform. Look for providers that follow proper identity verification processes and operate with licensed financial partners. Features such as two-factor authentication, transaction alerts, spending limits, and the ability to instantly freeze your card add an important layer of protection.


**Contactless payments.** Some virtual cards can be added to mobile wallets like Apple Pay or Google Pay, allowing you to make contactless payments with your phone. This can be particularly useful when travelling or making in-store purchases abroad. If this feature matters to you, make sure the card supports mobile wallet integration in your region.


Taking a few minutes to compare these factors can help you choose a virtual card that fits your spending habits and avoids unnecessary fees or payment issues later.


## The top virtual cards in Egypt for online payments


While cards issued by local banks work well for domestic spending, they are not always reliable for international payments. Here is a list of the top virtual cards in Egypt for online payments.


### Grey


[Grey offers virtual cards](https://grey.co/cards) linked to a[multi-currency account](https://grey.co/en-eg) that supports USD, EUR, and GBP. You can create multiple cards for various uses to properly plan your finances. One card can be for online shopping while another could be for subscriptions and or online course. Grey cards are globally accepted and works with the full range of international platforms


You can receive international payments into your Grey USD, GBP, or EUR account or fund your account in EGP and convert to USD to spend on your cards directly.


**Fees:** Grey virtual USD cards cost a one-time creation fee of $4, plus a minimum of $1 to fund the card, totalling $5 to get started. There are no monthly maintenance fees.


### EverTry


EverTry offers a solution for international payment restrictions in Egypt through their virtual dollar card platform. It allows Egyptian users to pay for global services that often decline local bank cards. It supports funding in local currency and USDT, making it accessible to users who are comfortable with crypto. The card works across a wide range of international platforms, including Netflix, Spotify, AWS, DigitalOcean, Namecheap, Facebook Ads, and Google Ads.


**Fees:** Card creation typically costs $2.5, with no monthly maintenance fees.


### Card-Y


Card-Y is a fintech platform that offers multi-currency global accounts with a linked virtual card, designed for Egyptian freelancers and remote workers. It offers USD and EUR account details for receiving international payments, with a free virtual card included that draws from those account balances. It also issues local Egyptian bank cards to subscribers.


**Fees:** Card-Y offers virtual Mastercard issuance for a $20 USD fee, which is valid for one year and does not add to the card balance. The service features a $1 monthly maintenance fee, a 1% USD transaction fee ($1 min/$5 max), and a 1.5% foreign currency conversion fee.


### Fyatu


Fyatu provides instant virtual Mastercards with support for multiple currencies, aimed at users who need to make global payments and manage international subscriptions. Onboarding is digital, and card issuance is immediate. It is a straightforward option for users whose primary need is an international spending card rather than a full suite of banking features.


**Fees:** Fyatu virtual card costs include a 1.5% fee for card usage (for either withdrawal or payments), with card replacement fees of $5 for World cards and $10 for Platinum cards. A $1.00 fee applies to declined transactions. Funding methods vary, with fees such as 3% for MTN MoMo and various percentages for online wallets like PayPal (3.5% + $0.30).


### AstroPay


AstroPay is a globally recognised digital wallet and virtual card platform, available in over 150 countries, including Egypt. It has been around since 2009 and has a particularly strong footprint in emerging markets across Africa, Latin America, and Asia. The platform supports more than 50 currencies, issues virtual prepaid cards instantly, and does not require a traditional bank account to sign up.


For Egyptian users, AstroPay works as a prepaid spending tool. You load funds onto your wallet using a local payment method, then use the virtual card for international purchases on platforms that accept Visa or Mastercard. Card details are issued instantly through the app, and the platform supports one-time or multi-use cards depending on the denomination.


However, bank withdrawals from AstroPay can attract fees of up to 6% depending on the institution. There is a margin of 1% to 3% on exchange rate.


**Fees:** No card purchase or maintenance fee. No annual fee. Transaction fees of 2–5% depending on the payment method used. FX markup of approximately 1–3% on non-native currency transactions. Withdrawals to a bank account: up to 6%.
